text:
incident-bot: ALERT: synthetic probe 'synth-generate-p99' firing repeatedly in us-west (312 firings in last 5m). Paging oncall. INC-2026-4827 created.
Sara H.: ack — I'm awake, looking now. can someone pull the probe query and the recent dashboard?
Jamal R.: on it. paging @Sara H. and @Kevin L. grabbing logs from the us-west probe cluster.
Kevin L.: I can see a sharp jump in tail latency for the generate endpoint on a subset of hosts (gp-2 pool). no 5xx spikes in backend yet.
Sara H.: sharing probe query from prometheus — helps to see numerator/denominator quickly:
```
sum(rate(redwood_probe_failures_total{probe="synth-generate-p99",region="us-west"}[5m])) by (instance)
/
sum(rate(redwood_probe_runs_total{probe="synth-generate-p99",region="us-west"}[5m])) by (instance)
```
Sara H.: failure ratio peaked ~0.12 on two instances. instances show high p99 for model x-small.
Trinh N.: there's also a quarter-hour cron hitting the same backend for batch indexing — looks like overlap window. could be synthetic + cron collision.
Jamal R.: any customer-facing errors reported?
Kevin L.: checked support queue — no 5xx complaints, but two dedicated customers in us-west reported slower responses (200–400ms extra). not global.
Sara H.: I think this is noisy probe firing due to cron overlap + transient host contended CPU. mitigation options: mute probe, add debounce, or relax threshold. I'm going to mute the probe for a short window while we triage.
Sara H.: `/monitoring mute synth-generate-p99 --region=us-west --duration=30m --reason="cron overlap + noisy firings"`
incident-bot: MUTE applied to probe synth-generate-p99 (us-west) for 30m — reason: cron overlap; linked INC-2026-4827.
Jamal R.: good move. For longer term, recommend: increase window to 5m, require consecutive failures=3, and bump threshold to 0.08 failure ratio. That should reduce false positives from single spike events.
Kevin L.: I'd prefer debounce over threshold bump — require 3 consecutive failure buckets so we don't hide real regressions.
Sara H.: creating temporary override rule now:
```
probe: synth-generate-p99
region: us-west
failure_threshold: 0.08
consecutive_failures: 3
window: 5m
```
Sara H.: applying to staging then rolling to prod for us-west.
Trinh N.: I'll add jitter to the synthetic schedule (randomize start within ±60s) and add a protection to avoid synthetic running during heavy cron windows.
Jamal R.: also adding a dashboard panel to correlate probe failure ratio with backend 95p latency and CPU steal on the host. propose alert only fire if both probe ratio > 0.06 AND backend 95p increased by >25% in same 5m window.
Kevin L.: agree — correlation check will cut noise. I'll draft the Grafana panel query and the alert rule.
Sara H.: quick customer-impact note: small latency bump for two dedicated customers on us-west-2; filed support notes. No data loss, no request failures.
Trinh N.: handoff plan: I'll take the follow-up investigation. pulling logs and host metrics to determine if it's contention or model warm-up issue. Handoff scheduled at 2026-04-02T07:00Z -> @Trinh N.
incident-bot: Handoff reminder: INC-2026-4827 -> Trinh N. (next oncall).
Jamal R.: creating followup ticket RDW-9875: "synth probe suppression + dashboard correlation" with checklist: jitter schedule, consecutive_failures default=3, dashboard panel, runbook entry.
Kevin L.: short ops-doc snippet being added to the runbook: how to mute a probe, when to increase window vs debounce, and when to escalate to SRE. uses examples and commands.
Sara H.: marking paging cleared for now — muting buy us time. Will post a short summary in #incidents after handoff. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT update: paging resolved; 1 temporary mute applied; 1 probe rule adjusted (staged).
Trinh N.: on postmortem I'll include the exact prometheus/grafana queries and the timeline. plan to propose permanent rule: default consecutive_failures=3 for all high-frequency probes and a global jitter on schedules.
Jamal R.: no objections. thanks for quick triage.
Sara H.: nice coordinated response. Leaving notes in the ticket and closing active page. :thumbsup:
